Counting it as a component gives it keep/remove/simplify decisions against A1, which have no meaning for a baseline. The test comment (ablation-report.bats:189) calls these arms "control arms" while counting them as components, which contradicts itself. It should be excluded like BARE/CONTROL, or handled as a second H1-style baseline contrast.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1913 — Excluding eval_only arms from `components` also drops them from detail_arms (line 2003) and from the sensitivity rows (line 1683). Nothing in the report ever shows a1_full_openmount's per-arm figures or its delta against a1_full. Only a row count is left on the oracle sensitivity "reported" line. The open-mount oracle A/B that this arm exists for has no output. It needs its own non-deciding section instead of disappearing silently.
head/evals/tests/ablation-report.bats:342 — The components come from the current suite and are applied to every suite_version partition, so suite v1 (which never ran the cycle-131 arms) now carries 9 decisions: three phantom no-rows/inconclusive entries. The test bumps 6 → 9 to match, which locks that behaviour in when it should catch it. Components should be scoped to the arms a partition's suite version actually declares or ran.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:117 — The pre-registered rules block (D-A5, "mirrored in NOTES before the first run") still says "expected false positives at 0.90 over 6 components", while the report now prints 9 and quotes this block verbatim in its Method section (AR-12). The report now contradicts itself. Growing the component family after registration is also a protocol change, and it needs a recorded decision and an updated rules/NOTES mirror, not just a code change.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:100 — a1_review_only names took_effect rule `review_only_phases`, and a1_no_dissent (line 103) names `no_review_dissent_envelope`. Neither rule is defined or referenced anywhere in the base tree, and took-effect.sh is not part of this PR. If the rules don't exist, the new validate-suite rule-id check fails on the committed suite (VS-14/VS-16), and every trial of these arms gets a took-effect miss, which becomes infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. Either add the rules in this PR or show they already exist.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:258 — The eval_only refusal runs before the existing REFUSAL classification (undeclared / absent / task_types mismatch). Outside the batch context, an eval_only arm on a build task reports "eval_only arm outside an evaluation batch" instead of the real task_types refusal. Inside it, that same arm still takes the REFUSAL path. The two refusals should be ordered consistently, with the structural refusal first.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:341 — The dry-run `config_edits` line is a hand-written copy of apply_arm_toggles' config mapping (companion_voice/gates/dissent/flatline). It is built from the raw suite toggles, not resolve_arm_toggles. Nothing ties it to lib/sandbox-mount.sh, so the dry run can describe edits the real run doesn't make. The tests only compare it to itself. The plan should come from the library, or be tested against it.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:87 — The rule-id set is scraped with a regex that only matches `rule_<id>() {` on a single line at column 0. A rule written as `function rule_x`, `rule_x ()`, or with the brace on the next line is invisible, and every arm naming it gets a false "unknown rule id" violation. Ask took-effect.sh for its rules (e.g. a --list-rules mode) instead of grepping its source.
head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:161 — The arm schema check validates `toggles`, `took_effect` and `eval_only`, but not the arm-level `effort` (a0_bare / a0_bare_fable `effort: high`, which pipeline-run.sh prefers over toggles.effort) or `phases`. A typo in either still passes the validator and only fails at run time.

Either the description over-claims, or part of the sprint is missing from this PR.
